transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The Hotpoint TCM580GUK is typically a condenser tumble dryer (it collects water in a tank rather than venting outside). The combination of poor drying and the top getting very hot strongly suggests restricted airflow. When air can't flow freely through the drum, heat builds up inside, which makes the casing feel hot but prevents the clothes from drying effectively. The most common cause is a blocked lint filter or condenser unit. Please check these first: clean the main lint filter in the door opening and remove the condenser unit (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front) to rinse off any fluff under the tap. Let it dry completely before refitting. Could you confirm if this is indeed a condenser model (does it have a water tank?) and let me know if the filters were blocked or clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]

Thank you. Yes, it's a condenser model with a water tank, and the water container was about half full and emptied fine. The door filter had a thick layer of fluff on it, and the condenser at the front bottom had lint packed on the fins, but it looked much cleaner after I rinsed it. The top panel does get very hot, and I often run the dryer while I'm out at work.

[Heading: Restricted airflow causing overheating and poor drying]
You’ve done the right thing by cleaning those filters. The thick fluff layer was definitely restricting airflow, which trapped heat inside (making the top hot) and stopped the air from drying your clothes properly. However, because it ran so hot while you were out, there is a chance the internal thermal safety cut-out has tripped or the moisture sensors are still affected.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
Thanks. Is there anything else I should check, or is it safe to keep using it now the filters are cleaned? It's about 12 to 14 years old and came with the house, so I don't know its history.

[Heading: Airflow restriction (filters)]
It is generally safe to use again provided you empty the water tank regularly (every cycle) and keep those filters clean. Please run a standard cotton programme for about 15 minutes with a small load of dry towels. Check if the drum gets warm/hot inside and if the clothes are drying effectively. If it still takes ages or feels cold inside after this, there may be an internal fault like a failed heating element or tripped thermal cut-out that requires an engineer.
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer not drying properly — what to check" — Poor drying is most often caused by restricted airflow. Clean the fluff filter every cycle, clean the condenser regularly and avoid overloading the drum — these are safe checks you can do yourself. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]

Thank you. I haven't done a test run since cleaning it, but before I cleaned the filters the drum was turning and heating, it was just very slow to dry. Is there anything else I should know about running it while I'm out at work, given how hot the top gets?

[Heading: Restricted airflow (resolved)]
Now that the filters are clear, the dryer should operate normally without excessive external heat. 1. Ensure the water tank is empty and correctly seated before starting.
2. 3. Do not overload the drum; a moderate load allows air to circulate properly.
4. If the top becomes uncomfortably hot or smells of burning during any cycle, stop using it immediately and call an engineer. With regular cleaning of the lint filter and condenser unit every few cycles, this 12–14 year old dryer should continue to work safely.
